newsitem.title: GERMANY: F.O. LICHT - Daily sugar report.
newsitem.headline: F.O. LICHT - Daily sugar report.

text.p: The following is a direct contribution from statistician F.O. Licht in Ratzeburg, Germany. Please address any queries to Helmut Ahlfeld on +00 49 4541 88920.

White sugar futures in London ended slightly firmer in quiet dealings. Most active March added $4 to close at $301.60 per tonne while May added $1 to close at $301.10 per tonne. There were no fresh news to influence prices. In New York speculators made yet another attempt to push up prices but buying interest quickly petered out once industry resistance materialized. Without fresh enduser demand prices are likely to remain in the doldrums. March lost 5 points to close at 10.57 cents/lb, while May gave up 2 points to close at 10.66 cents/lb. FUNDAMENTALS

UNITED KINGDOM - Sugar imports in October 1996, the first month of the 1996/97 campaign (October/September), amounted to 136,443 tonnes, raw value, slightly up on last year's 135,540 tonnes. Total imports in 1995/96 reached 1.320 million tonnes compared to 1.468 million tonnes in 1994/95 and 1.336 million tonnes in 1993/94. Major countries of origin in October 1996 were Mauritius with 50,535 tonnes raws against 83,605 tonnes, Fiji with 39,900 tonnes against 20,846 tonnes and Guyana with 37,100 tonnes, up from 18,600 tonnes. Sugar exports in October 1996 amounted to 31,490 tonnes, up from 26,816 tonnes exported in October 1995. Total exports in 1995/96 reached 390,747 tonnes compared to 560,076 tonnes in 1994/95. Major countries of destination in October 1996 were Israel with 12,562 tonnes whites against 7,961 tonnes, Norway with 4,099 tonnes, down from 4,585 tonnes and Italy with 2,754 tonnes compared to 2,934 tonnes.

PORTUGAL - Sugar imports in September 1996 amounted 35,485 tonnes, raw value, up from last year's 30,726 tonnes. This brought cumulative imports in the first three quarters of 1996 (January/September) up to 227,494 tonnes compared to 238,206 tonnes in the like period the previous year. Total imports in 1995 amounted to 312,542 tonnes compared to 340,710 tonnes in 1994. Major countries of origin in January/September 1996 were Swaziland with 43,041 tonnes raws against 35,362 tonnes, Zimbabwe with 31,747 tonnes, up from 27,150 tonnes and Jamaica with 31,756 tonnes against nil. Sugar exports in September 1996 amounted to 564 tonnes which brought cumulative exports in January/September 1996 up to 12,282 tonnes against 6,523 tonnes in the like period the previous year. Total exports in 1995 reached 15,432 tonnes, up from 7,434 tonnes in 1994. The major country of destination in 1996 was Spain with 8,696 tonnes whites against 2,723 tonnes.

Syria's General Foreign Trade Organization for Chemicals and Foodstuffs (GEZA) bought 26,000 tonnes of white and raw sugar for delivery between February 15 and March 17. 13,000 tonnes of white sugar were bought from the Japanese company Tomen at $344 per tonne and the other cargo of 13,000 tonnes of raws was bought from French trader Lorico at $290.40 per tonne. Turkey's 50,000 tonnes sugar export tender has been awarded to two local companies, trade sources said. The sugar will be delivered from the refineries at Elbistan, Agri, Kars, Bor and Carsamba. Further details were not immediately available. Turkey's state sugar company Turkseker said that Iraq had rejected its offer of 50,000 tonnes of white sugar for $390 per tonne because Baghdad found the price too high. Turkey offered the sugar, whose quality was not specified, in December under a UN formula which allows Iraq to sell oil worth $2 billion to buy food and medicine.
